holidays.name: National Carrot Cake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the moist, spiced, cream-cheese-frosted cake that lets you eat vegetables for dessert and feel virtuous about it. Bakers and dessert fans mark the occasion with slices, cupcakes, and plenty of walnut debates.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday popularized by food-day calendars and social media. Carrot cakes trace back to medieval Europe, when sugar was expensive and carrots were used as a sweetener.
holidays.funFact: Carrot cake became hugely popular in the United States in the 1970s, and carrots were used in puddings in medieval Europe because sweeteners were scarce and costly.

holidays.name: National Missing Persons Day Awareness / Women Physicians Day
holidays.description: National Women Physicians Day honors the achievements of women in medicine and the trailblazing doctors who fought to get into medical schools and hospitals.
holidays.origin: The observance is held on February 3 to commemorate the birthday of Elizabeth Blackwell, born in 1821, who became the first woman in the United States to earn a medical degree.
holidays.funFact: Elizabeth Blackwell was reportedly admitted to Geneva Medical College after the male student body voted on her application, apparently thinking it was a joke.

holidays.name: The Day the Music Died Remembrance
holidays.description: Music fans remember the 1959 plane crash that took the lives of Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and J.P. 'The Big Bopper' Richardson. Fans hold tribute concerts, play their records, and sing 'American Pie' with great gusto.
holidays.origin: The name comes from Don McLean's 1971 song 'American Pie,' which described February 3, 1959 as 'the day the music died.' The crash happened near Clear Lake, Iowa.
holidays.funFact: The Surf Ballroom in Clear Lake, Iowa, where the three stars played their last show, still hosts an annual tribute concert and is a pilgrimage site for rock and roll fans.

holidays.name: Setsubun (Bean-Throwing Festival)
holidays.description: In Japan, people throw roasted soybeans out of their doors while shouting 'Oni wa soto! Fuku wa uchi!' which means 'Demons out! Good luck in!' Some people wear demon masks so the neighbors can pelt them with beans.
holidays.origin: Setsubun marks the day before the beginning of spring in the traditional Japanese calendar. The ritual dates back centuries to Heian-era Japan, when ceremonies were held to drive away evil spirits at the turn of the season.
holidays.funFact: Tradition says you should eat one roasted bean for each year of your age, plus one more for good luck, so older people have to do a lot of crunching.

holidays.name: Feed the Birds Day
holidays.description: A day to put out seeds, suet, and snacks for hungry wild birds during the cold winter. Backyard birders get an excuse to buy yet another feeder and call it a good deed.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance tied to Saint Anthony's patronage in some traditions and to the wintertime need to help wild birds survive. It is also linked to the Mary Poppins song 'Feed the Birds (Tuppence a Bag).'
holidays.funFact: In the Disney film Mary Poppins, 'Feed the Birds' was reportedly Walt Disney's favorite song from the Sherman Brothers, who often played it for him at the end of the day.
